item.content:encoded:
I can't - quite - get behind this one. I like the concept a lot(I enjoy steampunk), but a couple bits of the execution just kind of kick this in the teeth, I feel.

Thoughts
– hide block

Each mast has a device on the end that projects a "bubble" which warps space around it in a way that does not match current spacetime theories.

This implies we've done enough testing on them to have some idea what they do/how they function. Why is there not more about this going on? This is great. Missed opportunity.

SCP-852-2 is a mummified Caucasian male wearing a pressure suit of primitive manufacture, resembling a diving helmet and suit but with a supplementary air tank and ventilation to remove excess carbon dioxide.

More a nitpick, there's no reason for this guy to be -2. Should be -1, since there isn't one already.

SCP-852 was originally located on Mare Imbrium approximately seven kilometers from the lunar outpost.

What outpost? This may just be my ignorance, but last I checked we don't HAVE an 'outpost' on the moon, so this feels like it needs clarification. Is this a Foundation outpost? I'm happy to buy that, but it needs to be said.

Analysis of the scene showed that SCP-852-2 met with unknown hostiles, which first severed the hoses of the suit, then shot SCP-852-2 in the back while he fled, piercing the suit and killing him either by trauma or asphyxiation. While the tracks made by SCP-852-2 are readily apparent, there are no tracks or any other evidence of the assailants.

This is the really big one. This is not how that works. If there's no evidence of the assailants, it A) cannot be shown that there were hostiles, unknown or otherwise, and B) introduces possibilities outside this scenario.

Hoses cut and something punching through his back? Any number of things could cut the hoses, anomalous or otherwise - like the spacetime bubble of the ship maybe - to create the weird mirror-edges, and instead of being shot in the back…he's on a moon with no atmosphere. Tiny meteoroids and other debris are constantly flying around space, and easily capable of hitting him, although this may be getting into 'never tell me the odds' territory.

In short, it doesn't feel believable, mostly due to lack of information/bad assumptions from supposed scientists.

item.content:encoded: He could have suffocated prior to bleeding out, or bled out prior to asphyxiating. There's no way to tell which of the two life-threatening situations he was in finished him off. We know that both of them happened to him, but finding out exactly how he spent the last moments of his life would be near impossible, especially given the damage that the remains would have sustained.

item.content:encoded:
There are actually other factors that are the reason for this design. The inventor of the craft thought he was conforming to the known physics of the time, but the physics that he thought he'd been using were disproved and replaced by general relativity. Thus, the craft had to be constructed no later than the turn of the twentieth century. The craft does not run on steam at all, of course, but battery power.

The alternate name for this vessel is Aetheric Spacecraft, but I didn't want to hit people over the head with either Jules Verne or the Sons of Ether from Mage: the Ascension. I wanted something different.

Still adjusting the sights.
